physicalNotes: Radius 0.13114484 Jupiter radii from Castro-González et al. 2022 (2022MNRAS.509.1075C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022MNRAS.509.1075C/abstract): 9,375.8 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00869 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.shape: Castro-González et al. 2022 (2022MNRAS.509.1075C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CASTRO_GONZ_AACUTE_LEZ_ET_AL__2022): a/R* 48.36; Mayo et al. 2018 (2018AJ....155..136M), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname MAYO_ET_AL__2018): inclination 89.46643 degrees

sources.phase: Castro-González et al. 2022 (2022MNRAS.509.1075C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CASTRO_GONZ_AACUTE_LEZ_ET_AL__2022): transit mid-time 2457148.5253369 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 8 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
